labels.label: ex:take_closed_unit_disc

hypotheses.paper: X the closed unit disc of R^2, the open disc identified with the Poincare disc
hypotheses.note: ClosedDisc = closedBall (0:C) 1; PoincareDisc = ball (0:C) 1 with hypDist := mathlib's UpperHalfPlane distance through the Cayley transform; cosh d = 1 + 2|z-w|^2/((1-|z|^2)(1-|w|^2)) (cosh_hypDist)

hypotheses.paper: G the group of isometries of the Poincare disc
hypotheses.note: HypIsom = all hypDist-preserving permutations of the open disc; classified: each is z -> (u s(z) + a)/(1 + conj(a) u s(z)), s = id or conj (HypIsom.exists_mobF, via the rotation/reflection classification at 0, eq_mul_sigmaB_of_hypRatio)

hypotheses.paper: G acts by homeomorphisms on X
hypotheses.note: MulAction HypIsom ClosedDisc by the continuous extension (extFun), ContinuousConstSMul; (G,X) analytical (faithful, rigid: HypIsom.eq_one_of_fix), AnalyticStructure; X locally unloopable (standing l.1660)
M Hausdorff, locally path-connected, first countable, connected (what is used); the genus is not used; second countability not used
S finite carried; 2g-2+s>0 not used (it is the condition for the metric to exist)

hypotheses.paper: M\S endowed with a hyperbolic metric
hypotheses.note: a (Isom(H),H)-structure on M\S: ChartedSpace PoincareDisc + HasGroupoid (gxGroupoid HypIsom PoincareDisc). The equivalence with a Riemannian metric of curvature -1 is not formalized (no Riemannian surfaces at this pin)

IsCompleteHyperbolic: every developing map of the universal cover is a covering map (Thurston/Goldman completeness of a (G,X)-structure); then it is a homeomorphism onto H (IsCompleteHyperbolic.exists_homeomorph). Metric completeness => covering (Hopf-Rinow for (G,X)) not formalized

a cusp at every s in S (CuspChart + IsHyperbolicCusp: V = phi^{-1}(ball(0,e^{-2 pi c})), s -> 0, and w -> phi^{-1}(e^{2 pi i w}), Im w > c, is a (G,H)-morphism from the horoball). The thick-thin step (finite volume complete => each end is a cusp) is not formalized

findings: l.1880 'with injective developing map': true for EVERY developing map of \widetilde M (they differ by G), not only for one (proved: take_closed_unit_disc).

l.1881 'an open neighborhood U of a singular point x ... is homeomorphic to {r<r_0}' holds for arbitrarily small such U (x to the apex), not for every open neighbourhood; and the singular points of \widetilde M are exactly the points over S = sing(M) (proved: a point over a cusp has horodisc neighbourhoods, so no chart of p^*B contains it).
l.1882 'D(U) is a horodisc centered at D(x)': D(U) is the horodisc together with its centre D(x) in the boundary circle (x in U); it is this set that is not open in X.
questions: ex:take_closed_unit_disc (l.1878): may 'M\S endowed with a finite volume complete hyperbolic metric' be read, for the example, as its (G,X) content: a complete (Isom(H),H)-structure (developing maps covering maps) with a cusp neighbourhood at each point of S (the parabolic model w -> phi^{-1}(e^{2 pi i w}) on {Im w > c})? Under that reading every assertion of the example is proved with no sorry; the Riemannian-metric-to-(G,X) translation, Hopf-Rinow completeness and the thick-thin decomposition (finite volume => cusps) are not formalized.

kb_proposals: Dot notation on a def whose body is a Pi type (IsCompleteHyperbolic) fails (kb/0010): call IsCompleteHyperbolic.exists_homeomorph H.complete ... explicitly.
An element type of a Subgroup has head Subtype, so g.foo dot notation fails; wrap it: abbrev HypIsom : Type := ↥hypIsomSubgroup, then HypIsom.foo works.
A set-builder {x | (x : ℂ) = ...} with x meant in a subtype elaborates x : ℂ and silently coerces the other side's Set ↥t to Set ℂ: always write {x : ClosedDisc | ...}.

Local notation for UniversalCover (Sᶜ : Set M) y₀ inside a section with variables gave 'unknown identifier' / internal exception #3 on later variables (and Θ clashes with asymptotics notation): spell the types out, avoid Θ.

To build a homeomorphism between {a} ∪ i(P) and {b} ∪ j(P) for open embeddings with matching neighbourhood bases, use GX.exists_homeomorph_insert (scaffold/GXScaffold/Hyperbolic/Plane.lean); it gives the D_∞ local models of Fox ends.
The Fox ends of \widetilde M over a cusp: GX.exists_end_lift identifies e(W_t) with L({Im w > t}) for one lift L of the cusp map; GX.basicSet_eq_insert gives basicSet W_t (e W_t) = {e} ∪ ι(e(W_t)).
notes: New scaffold module GXScaffold.Hyperbolic.Plane (2730 lines, 0 sorry, axioms propext/Classical.choice/Quot.sound for all main decls: campaign/WP-35i/Axioms.lean). It imports GX.SingularII.Tame and mathlib's UpperHalfPlane metric and Arcosh only; built with `taskset -c 0-11 lake build GXScaffold.Hyperbolic.Plane` (no upstream rebuild). Every conclusion of ex:take_closed_unit_disc is proved: Isom(H) built and classified, its action on the closed disc by homeomorphisms, (G,X) analytical and X locally unloopable, M a singular (G,X)-manifold with sing(M) = S (parabolic holonomy), M tamely singular, every developing map of \widetilde M injective, singular points of \widetilde M = points over S, each with arbitrarily small neighbourhoods homeomorphic to {r<r_0} in D_∞ (DInfty of GX.Singular.Quotient) mapped by D onto a horodisc with its centre, not open in X (reusing GX.not_isOpen_horodisc_insert of Tame). The row stays partial (unmarked) only because the hypothesis 'finite volume complete hyperbolic metric' is read as a complete (G,H)-structure with cusps (question): the thick-thin decomposition and Hopf-Rinow are not built; if the author accepts the reading (DEC-71 asks to build 'the developing map of a complete hyperbolic surface onto H^2, cusps', which this file does), the row can be marked closed. No inhabitant with a cusp is constructed (SCOPE (c)). Extends namespace GX only; no name clashes with GX/ or scaffold/ (checked). kb/0025: the new module must be added to the scaffold root's imports by the master session (WP-35i may not edit existing files) to be seen by the axiom sweep.
